summary: Yes. cache.py:20 (TTLCache.get) expires only when clock()-stored > ttl, so at exactly ttl the value is still returned (observed: ttl=10, fake clock, t=10 -> 'v', t=10.001 -> miss). Originally '>=' (d6cba38); 2e2afb8 'Keep cache entries through their last second (#12)' made it strict. Direct reason from commit message: coarse monotonic clocks (15 ms ticks) expired ttl=1 entries on first read after one tick; ttl is a guaranteed minimum lifetime.
